resources.string:
BentoBar draws your items (network speed, timer, calendar, tools…) on the status bar. Android allows that only through an accessibility service.

With it on, BentoBar: reads the status bar's layout, to find free space for your items; reads where windows are on the screen, never what is in them, to hide for full-screen apps and panels and to keep your items matching the status bar; reads the colour of the status bar clock, so your items match it; and runs the system actions you pick in the Tools menu or as a Shortcut item, such as screenshot or lock.

It never reads what is in another app's window, and it doesn't watch your keyboard, mouse or touches. Nothing the service reads ever leaves your Googlebook: BentoBar never collects or shares it.

BentoBar goes online for five items only, and only after you set them up: Weather and Air quality & UV ask Open-Meteo about the city you search for (or, with My location, about where the device is, rounded to about 10 km), Exchange rates asks Frankfurter for the European Central Bank\'s reference rates, Flight asks AirLabs about the flight you enter, and US stocks asks Finnhub about the stocks you follow, the last two with a key of your own. BentoBar sends nothing else anywhere: not your layout, your calendar, your clipboard, your notifications, the camera\'s picture, what\'s playing or anything it measures. It has no accounts of its own, no ads and no analytics, and it sends its developer nothing. Its accessibility service reads the status bar (its layout and its clock\'s colour) and where windows are on the screen, never what is in them. Some items read more, each only while it is in use and only with the access you give it: Notification icons reads other apps\' notifications, Mirror shows the camera\'s picture, and with Usage access on BentoBar reads how much data and storage each app uses, for the Network and Storage menus, and for Screen time when the screen was on and which apps were in front. None of that is stored or sent.

Weather sends Open-Meteo the city you search for. For the forecast it sends the coordinates of the city you pick, rounded to about a kilometre: about every 30 minutes while the bar is on screen, and when you open its menu or press Refresh. With My location it sends where this device is instead, rounded to about 10 km: BentoBar asks Android for the approximate location only while such an item is in the bar or waits in Hidden to show for rain or snow, or while BentoBar\'s settings window is open, and keeps it and its forecast in memory only. Open-Meteo sees your IP address, as any website does, and may keep it in its logs for 90 days.
